location.text: Found at Aquarium of the Atlantic.

entries.title: Stingray Facts
entries.text:
Stingrays get their name from the venomous barbs in their tail. Ouch!

Please watch those fingers! Management is not responsible for any injuries.

The Stingray's mouth and nostrils make them look like they're always happy! 

Go on, flip one over and see for yourself!

Stingrays have no bones! Oooh spooky! Where did they go?

entries.title: Starfish Facts
entries.text:
The humble Starfish is neither a fish nor a star. Huh?!

They don't have a brain and see with their legs. Weird!

They are also notorious for their ability to regenerate missing limbs. Whoa!

We ask that patrons please refrain from dismembering the Starfish.

entries.title: Horseshoe Crab Facts
entries.text:
Like the Starfish, the Horseshoe Crab is not an actual horse, shoe, or a crab! How confusing...

Did you know they also have blue blood? Gross.

Their blood is also vital to the pharmaceutical industry. How practical!

They're also much older than the dinosaurs! Neat!

items.name: The Lone Vulture

location.text: Found at Aquarium of the Atlantic.

items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
A vulture has come to my city. He does not kill, but shepherds prey to their death. For what feast would there be in a quick and easy demise? No... For him, the feast is their struggle. Dessert is when the last glimmer of hope leaves their eyes.

He has yet to find his place. It's different here in the city, where a semblance of order keeps the ignorant populace at peace. Yet he has come here, and thus with a reason. Searching, yearning... for a nest to call his own.

Mother welcomes you, my child. This world would call you a monster. I would call you my own. I would give you a calling. Do you hear me, child? In destruction there is creation! Direct your impulses; channel them toward a higher pursuit! I can see the shape of it now... A venue for others like you, others with hunger. A place for them to be free!

In this, you shall never be alone again.

Mother welcomes you home, sweet Veracio.

items.name: A New World
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Things have been different since the painter's association dissolved. Well, who am I kidding? They've been different ever since the War. They didn't feel that different, thanks to the Munis holding everything together. But it makes sense they could only invent work for a dying profession so long. It doesn't matter what color your wall is anymore, only that it's still standing.

Despite it all, I'm grateful. Me and Pa are learning new skills. They need more hands to help patch up holes in City Hall, mop up floods, repair pipes. And I've resolved to ask the Forestry Division for arms training. Things are getting more dangerous around here.

I guess that means my old life has ended. But it's not over. Now I'm embarking on a new one. No matter what happens, my spirit will live on in the city I call home. In the hearts of those I care about. That gives me the strength to face this new world with my head held high.

No more looking back. Onward and upward.

Nick

items.name: No Place Like Home
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Tim,

When does helping become hurting? I know you have this "vision" with that hero complex of yours that you're going to save Atlantic City from collapsing in on itself and everyone will live happily ever after. But do you know where people live happily ever after? Fairytales. And if you take a look around, it's pretty damn obvious we aren't living in one.

I want to go home. I want to go back to the way things used to be. I'm not one adverse to change, but I've got eyes. I can see we're fighting a losing battle here. It's not weak to give up. You're falling into a sunk cost fallacy thinking you need to be mayor til the day you die just 'cause you've done it this long.

Half the battle is knowing when to let go.

Love,
Frieda

items.name: Nothing to see here
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Tim,

I received your letter a few days ago. While I appreciate your concern and willingness to reach out, I just wanted to assuage your concerns and assure you that everything is fine. Getting old is no walk in the park, but I'm fit as a fiddle, all things considered.

In the future, please be more careful with your efforts to "touch base." Such correspondences suggesting my absence or physical frailty could be highly detrimental to my organization should they arrive in the wrong hands. I'm sure you understand, being in a position of authority yourself.

I've been extremely busy with personal matters that have diverted my attention from keeping up public appearances. Nothing dire, don't worry, but still pressing. If you need anything from me, please contact my sister, Concerta. She will be handling my personal inquiries in my absence. You can trust her, she's practically an extension of myself!

Best regards,

Q

Do you reckon you could spare some meds and send them our way? I would be ever so grateful, deigning to return the favor in any way possible. Even sparing some of your highly respected medical professionals would be an enormous boon!

I very much appreciate your precious time in reading and, hopefully, replying to this correspondence.

Best wishes,

Mother Charlotte

items.name: Perimeter Breach
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Sloane,

I appreciate the work you do, you know that. It's no act of cowardice to put your life on the line to protect strangers, 'specially if those strangers don't care much for you. Keep that in mind for what I'm about to say.

Not telling me about the Overgrown in the train cars is unacceptable. Just because they're in the Casino Quarter doesn't mean you can let 'em lie. We made a pact to protect EVERYONE in this godforsaken city, not just the ones we like.

I know we're stretched thin and resources are scarce right now. I'm working on fixing that. But you need to get some rangers in there before someone inevitably waltzes by and gets torn apart by those damned plants.

-Tim

items.name: Rot
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Sometimes I think the plant monsters aren't just another mutation. Could they be the dead, the blood I've spilled? Even indirectly. They don't think, do they? But they've got guns, some of 'em, at least. Their eyes are empty, but their faces are so human. Uncanny. Can't let anyone know it's getting to me. Can't let the rock shatter.

I'm starting to sound like a madman, it's true. I saw Sloane shoot one the other day. One of the fast ones. It made this gurgling noise when it went down, but for a second, I thought I heard her voice. Her screams. Even I know it's impossible, but I can't deny my own senses. If I can't trust my own head, then who can I trust?!

Perhaps it was just my memory, coming back to haunt me.

items.name: Unnecessary Questions
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
T,

You'd think they'd let it go after all these years, but we still got a few of Carly's ex-fanboys sniffing around, asking why she hasn't come back by now. They're not buying the "shame" angle. One of them thinks he's some sort of journalist that aims to "expose the truth." It's probably all bluffing, considering he doesn't have a paper backing him.

I know you're probably tempted to just let this go, but I really don't think we should. The Family and the Showmen are ruthless. If these rumors start to catch, and trust me, they will, they'll weaken us. And then the others will use that as an excuse to get out of paying their dues. We'll go broke. Utilities will shut off, the Overgrown will spill in, the tourists will spill OUT, a lot of people will die, and Acee will crumble. That sound like a timeline you want?

Just give me the green light, and I'll take care of it. A journalist can't write without blood in his veins.

-B

items.name: Wild Child
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Anna,

If you decide to show your face in the Casino Quarter again, make sure you're wearing a mask. Words can't express the immeasurable disappointment your father and I cope with every day knowing you've sold yourself out to the Munis. I thought we raised you better than that! Where oh where did I go wrong...?

You could've had a nice life here. A bearable one, at least. Gotten married, settled down. Maybe there would've been some grandkids in that now dashed future... Dreams that will never come to fruition. But you gave that all away for a job that hardly pays you and will send you into an early grave. Foolishness!

What motivates you, I will never know. But I will warn you: Rumors here are vicious, and the Family doesn't take kindly to traitors. In short? Stop trying to visit us. Not even for our reputation's sake. For the sake of your own life.

Do you dispatch medics to cure broken hearts? God only knows I need it.

-Ma

items.name: Forgive Me
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Connie,
I'm sorry, but I can't face you in person. I lost it all.
I was at the casino last night, and was on a huge winning streak. I just kept betting more and more. I couldn't stop myself.
First I used up our saving, and then Steven's college fund. We were going to be millionaires with the return I was getting. I was going to take you to Hawaii to maybe repair our marriage. We were going to be happy again. And then I bet the house, and it all went down from there.
I'm so sorry Connie, but I lost it all. Rob at the pub doesn't even know I'm not even gonna be able to pay my tab.
The bank is probably going to be around to take the house within the week.
Please don't try and find me. Our marriage was rocky already, and I can't dare face you after this

items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
To whatever sweet, wonderful, caring soul may come across this letter...

You gotta get me outta here!

My name is Gene, I been held captive by the Family for... er... well, a good long while at least. Hard to remember when you're so full of Devil's Blood that you may as well be the Jersey Devil itself.

I'm a chem cook. Yeah, I said it! Damn near the best one in Atlantic City, too. Which is why they've had me makin' Blood for them for as far back as my very short term memory goes. Day and night, nothin' but cookin', cookin', cookin'. It's outta control! I got no privacy and no life!

So anyway, my daring, dashing heavily armed knight in shining armor... Come to my rescue, why don't ya?

I'll be waiting!
Gene

items.name: Just My Luck!
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Just my luck I'd be right back where I started.
This is why I left Coos Bay in the first place. I was tired of makin chems in that soggy ass flooded town, so I packed my bags and headed as far East as I could to get away from that shitshow. I actually thought I was doin good for the first time in my life.
Then I heard about a well payin job when I was in the DC ruins. Said it was in old Atlantic City. Sounded somethin fancy! Afterall, I heard they recovered well after everything went to shit. Well, turns out they needed someone to make this Devil's Blood stuff. Lucky me I'm damn good at this kind of work despite wantin to turn things around. Figure I'll do it for a while until I can save up some caps. Trouble is though, I'm not in some swanky safe place I thought I could call home, but instead it's in another god awful flooded coastal city! Now here I am, fightin' off mutated abominations in the same kind of shithole I hoped to leave behind!

items.name: Last Confession
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
How can I be absolved if there is no priest to stand before me? How can I seek forgiveness in a world that no longer cares if I am guilty or innocent? I don't wish for forgiveness from a deity, from a person, or from anything corporeal. I wish I could forgive myself, but that's impossible.

I look at what the Blood has done to my body, and I feel nothing at all. No anger, no sadness, simply an empty resignation. This city was like clay to me. I could've shaped it any way I wanted. Instead, I cut off my own hands.

All those miles traveled, all those lives wasted...just for the empire to fall. Sometimes, you can do everything right, and the world still falls apart around you anyway. Irregardless, it's not like I had all the time in the world left. If the Blood hadn't killed me, time would've taken me.

If Tony's reading this...please, do the right thing. Do it for me.

items.name: Not Enough
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Mother says the Blood unlocks our true potential. So what does it mean that I float in the same vast abyss? For a blissful moment, the waves glowed every color, soft as silk, and I drifted weightless in an empty paradise. I met the one called Peace for the first and only time.

Then, the cacophony. Lights glaring! Voices shouting! Walls crashing back to perspective! Gravity's blunt and shocking force! Everything louder than before. The face of Danger, wholly revealed, staring back endlessly from each and every surface... and still He has not closed his eyes.

Yet nothing has awakened in Me. I breathe more terrified than ever before. I stumble more often. I open my mouth and cannot find the words it grasped just a moment before. Is this all my potential? Am I so much a failure?

It cannot be, it cannot... I just need to dive deeper and find it. Yes... I must have glimpsed something at the bottom of that abyss. There must be something magnificent there! I just need more, more than we've ever been allowed... But where? How? Every well has a source. I must find it and drink. Deeply.

Then... Only then I will be magnificent.

Chapter 12 - Neapolitan Nitwit

While documenting the incredible journey of my life, It's important for me to document both my triumphs, and my failures. And boy howdy is this one triumphant failure.

I blew it though. She saw right through my bullshit, and caught me making a grab for the vault key. Last thing I see is the butt of a gun clocking me in the skull.

They kept me in a dark room and beat the names out of me. Soon as they started hitting the moneymaker, I cracked real quick. I have no regrets. That mafioso and that sorry Muni fella would have done the same. Frankly, I'm just grateful those thugs didn't break anything too important. I can get by on crutches for a long while.

I've been blacklisted from the Casino Quarter. So I'm heading back to Showmen's pier. Maybe they'll take pity on me and let me sing the opening to that game they're always running.

After writing it all out, maybe this one shouldn't make it to the autobiography.

items.name: To Tony
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Tony,

You're probably never going to read this, are you? It's the most hopeless feeling in the world, I tell you, just scribbling into the void while I can practically feel my body giving in from the inside out knowing that you'll never even lay eyes on this piece of paper.

I know you feel like you let me down, but the truth is, I let you down. I was supposed to watch your back, keep an eye out for you. I lost track of things, and it all started spiralling out of control. If I could turn back time, I would've burned that first shipment of Blood. But we both know I can't do that.

It's poisonous, the damn thing. It's like the sweetness of sugar coursing through your blood. But just like how sugar rots teeth, there's something about this chem that decays your blood, makes it ache. Everything that flows through me aches.

I should've been alive to hand the reins of la cosa nostra to you personally. I should've been well enough to stand up and declare your authority. But I wasn't. And it's all my fault.

I'm sorry, kid. I really am. I saw dollar signs, and in the end I screwed us both.

items.name: Unaccounted Blood
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Like I said, this stays between you and me Murph. I'm not saying anything out loud in case the joint's bugged, so be sure to burn this letter.

I played cards with some of the guys who deliver the daily earnings into the vault. There's a ton of caps sure, but one guy gave me a tip. Swears he saw a whole crate of Devil's Blood that remains unaccounted for in any of the logs. Some kind of clerical oversight.

Think about it Murph. An entire crate of the stuff just left behind. A crimson treasure ripe for the taking.

Even if someone got the Blood, not many folks are willing to fence the stuff. The Family's got an iron grip on the Devil's Blood brewing and distribution in Atlantic City. If anyone outside the Family tries to sell it, they're signing their own death warrant.

But there's a lot of caps in it for someone who can. That's where you come in Murph. I'm familiar with your work back in Nevada when there were casino's worth robbing. Can't think of anyone better to break in and lift the stash.

If you manage to get that crate out, I'll show you my magic trick where I turn Blood into caps.
